site.title: Grade 10 Computer Science
site.tagline: Lessons, videos and quizzes for our class. Work at your own pace; the site remembers where you stopped.

courses.title: Build your first web page
courses.summary: Learn how websites work, write HTML and CSS by hand, and put your own page on the internet.
courses.description: You'll start from a blank file and finish with a real web page that anyone can visit. No experience needed: just a browser and a text editor.
courses.subject: Web Development
outcomes: Explain what happens when you open a website
Write a page with headings, paragraphs, links and images
Style a page with colors, fonts and simple layouts
Publish your page for free with GitHub Pages

project.title: Final project: an About Me page
project.description: Build a one-page site about yourself or a hobby, publish it, and send your teacher the link.

modules.title: How the web works
modules.summary: What a browser does and the three languages of the web

lessons.title: What happens when you open a website
lessons.summary: Follow a web page from the address bar to your screen, and meet HTML, CSS and JavaScript.

lessons.title: Your first HTML page
lessons.summary: Write a complete page with headings, paragraphs, lists, links and images.

modules.title: Make it look good
modules.summary: Colors, fonts and layout with CSS

lessons.title: Styling with CSS
lessons.summary: Connect a stylesheet and change colors, fonts and spacing, including with classes.

lessons.title: Boxes and layout
lessons.summary: Understand the box model and line up elements side by side with flexbox.

lessons.title: Publish your page on GitHub Pages
lessons.summary: Put your page online for free with GitHub Pages and share the link.

courses.title: Python from zero
courses.summary: Write your first programs: store information, ask the user questions, make decisions and repeat work with loops.
courses.description: Python is one of the easiest programming languages to start with and one of the most used in the world. By the end you'll write a small number-guessing game.
courses.subject: Programming
outcomes: Run Python code in your browser or on your computer
Store and change information with variables
Make choices with if, elif and else
Repeat steps with for and while loops

project.title: Final project: a guessing game
project.description: Write a game where the computer picks a number and the player keeps guessing until they get it. Share your code with your teacher.

lessons.title: What is a program?
lessons.summary: Run your first line of Python, see how programs run top to bottom, and read error messages.

lessons.title: Variables and types
lessons.summary: Store values in variables and learn the difference between text, whole numbers, decimals and True/False.

lessons.title: Talking to the user
lessons.summary: Ask the user questions with input(), convert their answers to numbers, and print with f-strings.

modules.title: Decisions and repetition
modules.summary: Make your programs react and repeat

lessons.title: Making decisions with if
lessons.summary: Make your program choose what to do with if, elif and else, and combine conditions.

lessons.title: Repeating with loops
lessons.summary: Repeat work with for and while loops, then start building a number-guessing game.

courses.title: GitHub for beginners
courses.summary: Save every version of your work, collaborate without overwriting each other, and build a public portfolio of your projects.
courses.description: GitHub is where most programmers keep and share their code. You'll start in the browser with no installs, learn the branch and pull request workflow real teams use, then connect Git on your own computer.
courses.subject: Developer Tools
outcomes: Explain the difference between Git and GitHub
Create repositories and save changes as commits
Propose and merge changes with branches and pull requests
Plan work and collaborate using issues
Use Git on your own computer to clone, commit and push
Build a GitHub profile that shows off your projects

project.title: Final project: your GitHub portfolio
project.description: Create a profile README, then improve it through a branch and a merged pull request. Send your teacher the link to your profile.

modules.title: Get started
modules.summary: What Git and GitHub are, and your first repository

lessons.title: What are Git and GitHub?
lessons.summary: Learn how Git tracks every version of your work and how GitHub adds teamwork on top.

lessons.title: Your account and first repository
lessons.summary: Create your account and a repository with a README, and find your way around it.

modules.title: Work in the browser
modules.summary: Commits, branches, pull requests and issues

lessons.title: Saving changes with commits
lessons.summary: Edit files in the browser, save them as commits, read the history and write good commit messages.

lessons.title: Branches and pull requests
lessons.summary: Work safely on a branch, propose changes with a pull request, then review and merge.

lessons.title: Issues and working together
lessons.summary: Track tasks with issues, close them from pull requests, invite teammates and fork projects.

modules.title: Work on your computer
modules.summary: Git on your own machine, and showing off your work

lessons.title: Git on your computer
lessons.summary: Install Git, then clone, commit, push and pull from your own computer.

lessons.title: Show your work with a profile
lessons.summary: Build a profile README and pin your best projects so others can see your work.

courses.title: Linux for beginners
courses.summary: Use the command line with confidence: move around the file system, manage files, install software and write your first script.
courses.description: Linux runs most of the internet, the core of every Android phone and all of the world's fastest supercomputers. You'll learn the command line from scratch, using a free Linux terminal on whatever computer you have.
courses.subject: Developer Tools
outcomes: Explain what Linux is and where it's used
Open a Linux terminal on Windows, Chromebook, Mac or in the browser
Move around the file system and manage files and folders
Read file permissions and use sudo safely
Install software with a package manager
Combine commands with pipes and write a simple script

project.title: Final project: your first shell script
project.description: Write a script called `about-me.sh` that greets the user by name, shows today's date and lists the files in the home folder. Make it executable, run it, and send your teacher a screenshot.

modules.title: Meet Linux
modules.summary: What Linux is and how to get a terminal

lessons.title: What is Linux?
lessons.summary: Find out what Linux is, what distributions are, and why the command line is worth learning.

lessons.title: Get a Linux terminal
lessons.summary: Open a Linux terminal on Windows, Chromebook, Mac or in your browser.

lessons.title: Your first commands
lessons.summary: Read the prompt, run your first commands and use shortcuts like Tab and Ctrl + C.

lessons.title: Finding your way around
lessons.summary: Move around the folder tree with pwd, ls and cd, using absolute and relative paths.

lessons.title: Creating and managing files
lessons.summary: Create, read, edit, copy, move and delete files and folders, and use wildcards.

lessons.title: Permissions and sudo
lessons.summary: Read file permissions, change them with chmod, and use sudo safely.

lessons.title: Installing software
lessons.summary: Install, update and remove software with the apt package manager.

lessons.title: Pipes, search and your first script
lessons.summary: Combine commands with pipes, search with grep and find, and write your first script.

courses.title: How to Write A Resume to Get Hired
courses.summary: Discover the art of creating a resume that stands out in the competitive job market and submit your resume to be reviewed by our industry experts.
courses.description: Discover the art of creating a resume that stands out in the competitive job market and submit your resume to be reviewed by our industry experts. You will receive direct, constructive feedback on your resume guiding you through developing compelling narratives to showcase your skills & experiences, maximizing your chances of being noticed and shortlisted by employers.
courses.subject: Career Skills
outcomes: Structure a clear resume with the sections employers expect
Turn everyday duties into achievements with measurable results
Tailor your resume to a specific job posting and its keywords
Format your resume so applicant tracking systems can read it
Use AI tools to improve your resume without losing accuracy or your own voice
Show transferable skills from school, volunteering and other experience

modules.title: How to Write A Resume to Get Hired

lessons.title: Refresh Your Resume
lessons.summary: Build, tailor and polish a professional resume using proven practices, AI tools and formatting that applicant tracking systems can read.

lessons.title: Project: Refresh Your Resume
lessons.summary: Apply what you learned by tailoring your resume to a real job posting, highlighting your achievements and transferable skills, and submitting it for feedback.
